slice: orchestration surface: daedalus/kairos/ (11), daedalus/lanes/ (5), daedalus/council/ (6), daedalus/providers/ (10)
summary: This slice is the orchestration surface: kairos plans and isolates work (scheduler, worktree, gated_writes), lanes holds the one shared write-lane guard baseline, council runs advisory cross-vendor deliberation, and providers are the vendor adapters. It is the healthiest-consolidated part of the repo on the anti-duplication axis -- lanes/ was an explicit de-duplication of per-provider guards and both write lanes (ollama, deepseek) now call the same run_checks; council/ enforces Invariant 4 structurally by having no approve/score field at all. The weakness is Gate-0 shaped, not design shaped: council/ and lanes/fanout perform real network egress, subprocess spawn and filesystem writes but have zero rows in daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py, and lanes/fanout is only reachable from unregistered tools/ scripts. There is also a live packaging hole -- daedalus.lanes is absent from pyproject.toml's explicit package list, so a non-editable install ships both write lanes importing a package that is not there. Three kairos modules (archive, evolution, shadow_shell) are test-only islands, and kairos/orchestrate.py is a second, unregistered CLI door.

Two parallel candidate-isolation mechanisms coexist: daedalus/spine/attempt.py:TaskAttempt (canonical, named as such by gated_writes.py's own docstring) and daedalus/kairos/shadow_shell.py + evolution.py (islanded, test-only). daedalus/council/bus.py is a second append-only hash-chained event log alongside the spine event store. AGENTS.md names 'another event store' a release-blocking defect. Advisory scope is a plausible exemption but it is stated nowhere in code or plan.

daedalus/council/vendors.py:41 deliberately does not use adapters.subprocess_adapter.RUNTIME_PROFILES, so there are two independent subprocess-hardening profiles for the same effect class, free to drift.

The council package's core control -- 'no approve/reject/score/consensus field exists' (council/__init__.py) -- is enforced only by convention. No test asserts the absence, so the one structural guarantee of Invariant 4 in this package can be dissolved by an ordinary commit.

LEGACY SHIM DUPLICATION confirmed for this slice's four kairos modules: daedalus/decompose.py:1, daedalus/drafts.py:1, daedalus/mission_control.py:1 and daedalus/orchestrate.py:1 are pure re-export wrappers over kairos/*, and grep finds no importer of any of them outside build/lib copies. daedalus/ikarus.py is the same shape over kairos/scheduler. Five 0-reference shims; safe deletion candidates that would also remove five ways to reach kairos without going through cli.

EXEMPLARY: daedalus/lanes/__init__.py's docstring is the best piece of engineering writing in the slice -- it states the measured 2026-07-30 failure (two guards landed in the paid lane and not the free one within the same hours, making the untrusted external lane strictly safer than the default local one), names the mechanism ('nobody decided that; it is what per-provider copies do'), and the module is the fix.

EXEMPLARY: daedalus/kairos/archive.py:3-15 is the attribution standard the repo should hold everywhere -- upstream URL, commit SHA, date, licence, the exact upstream line ranges taken, and an explicit list of what was deliberately NOT ported.

EXEMPLARY: daedalus/council/__init__.py's 'ABSENCE OF THE FIELD is the control' and 'advisory-by-docstring is not a control' -- the correct structural reading of Invariant 4, undermined only by having no test.

RISK, local lane graph conditioning is silently shed: providers/ollama.py:822-827 drops the structural brief FIRST when the estimated prompt exceeds the window. So the Gate 4 prior (graph-conditioned context helps) is unmeasurably applied on the default lane -- present on small tasks, absent on large ones, with no signal in the report. Any future budget-equal comparison on this lane is confounded until the shed is recorded.

The claude_cli lane -- the only can_write + trusted_with_ip + agentic provider -- explicitly ignores the policy argument (claude_cli.py, 'unused: Claude is agentic + trusted'). Every other lane runs lanes/checks.py. That is the intended trust model, but it means the shared write-lane baseline covers the two cheap lanes and not the privileged one.
